cards.name: CMYK conversion for press
cards.summary: RGB artwork and photos are converted to the printer's CMYK profile once, at the end, with out-of-gamut colours tamed first, so the press result matches the approved proof.
use_for: brochures, posters and packaging that started in RGB
avoid: screen, web or social output: stay in RGB
converting back and forth: every conversion loses colour; keep an RGB master and convert a copy
brand colours with official CMYK builds: type the official values instead of trusting a conversion
converting before the printer names a profile: ask first (coated, uncoated and newsprint profiles differ a lot)

steps.note: Edit > Color Settings: not run. It changes the application's colour settings, which this runner never does. Set the CMYK working space to the printer's profile by hand (manual).

Select > Color Range (script): Colors = Out Of Gamut (the 'outOfGamut' enum), Fuzziness 40. Ran; a probe showed a selection spanning most of the frame. It uses the CMYK working space Photoshop already had; View > Proof Setup is a view setting and is not touched. The settings-free route carries the probe's Reds, so the colours come from the script.
steps.script: var x = new ActionDescriptor(); x.putInteger(C2T('Fzns'), 40); x.putEnumerated(C2T('Clrs'), C2T('Clrs'), S2T('outOfGamut')); executeAction(tk('colorRange'), x, DialogModes.NO);

steps.note: Color and vibrance adjustment layer made while that selection is active, so the selection becomes its mask: Vibrance -10, Saturation -15. Ran. The step frame shows the strongest blue, purple and orange test bars toned down.

Edit > Convert to Profile (script: convertProfile): destination U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2, Relative Colorimetric, Black Point Compensation on, dither off. The settings-free route carries the probe's Adobe RGB, so the profile comes from the script. Ran; the final frame (converted back to RGB for the PNG) shows the saturated blue and purple bars duller than the input. The run's layer list ends as one Background in CMYK mode: the conversion flattened the layered file, so the vibrance layer is baked in (as the recipe says, run it on a copy and keep the RGB master). Untested: the printer's own profile and Perceptual intent for very saturated photos.
steps.script: d.convertProfile('U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2', Intent.RELATIVECOLORIMETRIC, true, false);

cards.name: Rich black vs 100K black
cards.summary: Large solid black areas print as a rich black build (for example C60 M40 Y40 K100) while body text, thin rules and barcodes stay pure 100K so they cannot misregister into coloured fringes.
use_for: black backgrounds and big black display type
posters and covers with large dark areas
keeping small type and barcodes crisp
avoid: rich black on small text, hairlines or barcodes: four plates must register exactly; use 100K
the 400 % registration black (C100 M100 Y100 K100): it never dries and smears; use the printer's build
exceeding the printer's total ink limit (often about 300 % on coated, lower on uncoated): ask for it
Photoshop photos: their black is already built by the CMYK conversion (GCR / UCR); do not repaint it

steps.note: Two global swatches: text and lines c0 m0 y0 k100; large areas and display type over about 24 pt c60 m40 y40 k100 (240 % total ink) or the printer's own build (doc.swatches.add(), swatch.color = new CMYKColor()).
Edit > Edit Colors > Overprint Black: Add Black, 100 %, Fill and Stroke, so the 100K text overprints instead of knocking out (dialog; DOM: fillOverprint / strokeOverprint = true).
Preferences > Appearance of Black: display and output all blacks accurately, so the screen shows the difference between 100K and rich black.

cards.name: Overprint black text and keylines
cards.summary: Black text, thin black keylines and trap strokes are set to overprint, so slight plate misregistration cannot open white gaps, and the result is checked in an overprint preview.
use_for: thin black outlines around coloured shapes
avoid: white or light objects: overprinting makes them disappear on press
coloured (non-black) objects over other colours: the inks mix into a new colour; preview first
RGB / screen work: overprint only matters in CMYK or spot separations
Photoshop: pixel layers have no overprint attribute; set it in the vector layout

View > Overprint Preview to see the inks mix as on press.

cards.name: Bleed and crop marks
cards.summary: Background art runs 3 mm (0.125 in) past the trim on every side, and the press PDF carries the bleed and crop marks.
avoid: important text or logos inside the bleed or close to the trim: keep a 3-5 mm safe zone
marks drawn inside the artboard: they get trimmed or printed; let the PDF export add them
screen-only output: bleed does not apply

steps.note: Image > Image Size (script: resizeImage with resampling off): 300 ppi, so the pixel count stays 1920 x 1080 and the picture becomes 6.4 x 3.6 in (162.6 x 91.4 mm). The settings-free route carries the probe's 200 px, so the values come from the script. Ran. This sets a print resolution so the 3 mm bleed is a realistic size.
steps.script: d.resizeImage(undefined, undefined, 300, ResampleMethod.NONE);

steps.note: Layer > New > Layer from Background (new step): ran, the artwork is a layer (labelled 'art') so the canvas can grow with a transparent border.

Image > Canvas Size (script: resizeCanvas, centre anchor): +6 mm width and height, 3 mm a side (about 35 px at 300 ppi). The settings-free route carries the probe's 500 x 400 px, so the size comes from the script. Ran; the new strip is transparent.
steps.script: d.resizeCanvas(UnitValue(d.width.as('mm') + 6, 'mm'), UnitValue(d.height.as('mm') + 6, 'mm'), AnchorPosition.MIDDLECENTER);

steps.note: Script (target 'art'; replaces the stretched copy of the first run, which ghosted the bottom type and showed seams at the trim): for each side the one-pixel edge row or column of the art is copied to its own layer (Layer Via Copy), stretched over the 3 mm bleed (35 px left and top, 36 px right and bottom) and merged back; the four corners are filled the same way from the corner pixel. Content-Aware Fill is not available for a selection on the canvas edge. Ran; the script reports the margins. The run shows the picture's edge colours smeared outward, with no repeated content and no seam at the trim; a smear is a plain extension, so detail near the edge is not continued.

Script (new step, target 'art'): the canvas grows another 4 mm per side (47 px) as a slug, a white 'paper' layer goes under the art, and eight crop marks (black, 2 px wide, 41 px = 3.5 mm long) are drawn on a 'crop marks' layer in the slug, each 35 px (the bleed) away from the trim and centred on a trim line, two per corner. The marks are drawn pixels, a stand-in for the marks a press PDF exporter adds; they sit outside the bleed so trimming removes them. Ran; the script reports canvas 2085 x 1245 px with the 1920 x 1080 px trim box at (82, 82).

Script (new step): saveAs a Photoshop PDF (layers off, preserve editing off) into the run's output folder as ps_bleed_marks.pdf. Ran; the script reports the file size and the page size it read back from the PDF: MediaBox 500.4 x 298.8 pt, which is 176.5 x 105.4 mm (the 162.6 x 91.4 mm trim plus 3 mm bleed and 4 mm slug on each side). It is an RGB Photoshop PDF without a PDF/X standard; its marks are the drawn pixels above.

File > Print > Printing Marks: not run. It sends output to the print system; Photoshop's print dialog is the only place it adds marks, and a script cannot set it. The marks in this plan are drawn in the slug instead (step 5). For marks added by the exporter itself, place the image in Illustrator or CorelDRAW and export a press PDF there (manual). The run is partial because of this step.

cards.name: Outline text for hand-off
cards.summary: Live type is converted to vector outlines (curves, shapes) in a copy of the file that goes to print, so missing or unembeddable fonts cannot reflow or substitute.
use_for: logos and display type sent to printers, sign makers and cutters
files opened on machines without the fonts
avoid: the working master: outlines cannot be turned back into text; keep a live-type copy
long body copy: it bloats the file; embed the fonts in a PDF/X instead
type that still needs corrections: finish the copy first

steps.note: On a saved copy: select the type (doc.textFrames) and Type > Create Outlines; DOM textFrame.createOutline() (id paired by its shortcut, not confirmed).

s.Move(0, 1.0)

copy.Fill.ApplyNoFill()

cards.name: Flatten transparency for press
cards.summary: Opacity, blend modes, soft shadows and glows are flattened into opaque pieces at press resolution for workflows that cannot take live transparency (PDF/X-1a, older RIPs).
use_for: spot-colour jobs with shadows or glows
avoid: the master file: flattening is destructive; keep transparency live and flatten a copy or at export
PDF/X-4 workflows: they keep live transparency, so nothing needs flattening
low flattener settings near text and thin lines: they rasterize or thicken; outline the text
judging CorelDRAW bitmap effects on a half-size preview: they lose pixel-scale detail; check at 1:1

The flattener preset for final press output (name only harvested).

PDF/X from an RGB Photoshop file without a destination profile and output condition: the save fails or falls back

steps.script:
import math
names = ("orange_box", "blue_star", "grad_circle", "pgd_type", "zigzag")
originals = [labels[k] for k in names]
copies = [labels[k].Duplicate(0, 0) for k in names]

def proof(c):
    """a colour taken through CorelDRAW's own RGB -> CMYK -> RGB conversion (the gamut of the CMYK profile)"""
    d = rgb("#%02X%02X%02X" % (c.RGBRed, c.RGBGreen, c.RGBBlue))
    d.ConvertToCMYK()
    d.ConvertToRGB()
    return d

def delta(a, b):
    return math.sqrt((a.RGBRed - b.RGBRed) ** 2 + (a.RGBGreen - b.RGBGreen) ** 2 + (a.RGBBlue - b.RGBBlue) ** 2)

flagged = []
for k, sh in zip(names, copies):
    worst = 0.0
    try:
        if sh.Fill.Type == 1:
            c = sh.Fill.UniformColor
            d = proof(c)
            worst = max(worst, delta(c, d))
            sh.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(d)
        elif sh.Fill.Type == 2:
            f = sh.Fill.Fountain
            for end in (f.StartColor, f.EndColor):
                d = proof(end)
                worst = max(worst, delta(end, d))
                end.CopyAssign(d)
    except Exception as e:
        print("fill skipped", k, e)
    try:
        if sh.Outline.Type != 0:
            oc = sh.Outline.Color
            d = proof(oc)
            oc.CopyAssign(d)
    except Exception as e:
        print("outline skipped", k, e)
    print(k, "largest colour shift", round(worst, 1))
    if worst > 45:
        flagged.append(k)
        sh.Outline.Width = 0.22
        sh.Outline.Color.CopyAssign(rgb("#FF00FF"))

def place(items, left):
    sr = app.CreateShapeRange()
    for it in items:
        sr.Add(it)
    g = sr.Group()
    k = 8.6 / g.SizeWidth
    g.SetSize(g.SizeWidth * k, g.SizeHeight * k)
    g.SetPosition(left, 9.6)
    return g

place(originals, 0.7)
place(copies, 10.7)
for text, x, size, col in (("Screen colours (RGB)", 0.7, 30, "#1A1A1A"), ("Press proof (CMYK, emulated)", 10.7, 30, "#1A1A1A")):
    t = layer.CreateArtisticText(0.0, 0.0, text, 0, -1, "Arial Black", size)
    t.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb(col))
    t.Outline.SetNoOutline()
    t.SetPosition(x, 10.9)
note = "Out-of-gamut colours flagged with a magenta outline: " + (", ".join(k.replace("_", " ") for k in flagged) or "none") + ". Each fill is taken RGB to CMYK and back with CorelDRAW's colour engine."
t = layer.CreateArtisticText(0.0, 0.0, note, 0, -1, "Arial", 17)
t.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#C0007A"))
t.Outline.SetNoOutline()
t.SetPosition(0.7, 4.0)
t2 = layer.CreateArtisticText(0.0, 0.0, "This is a stand-in for the View > Proof Colors preview (a window setting that no export shows). It is a preview, not a contract proof.", 0, -1, "Arial", 15)
t2.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#1A1A1A"))
t2.Outline.SetNoOutline()
t2.SetPosition(0.7, 3.4)
result = None

The screen colours are drawn on the left and the press proof on the right; any shape whose colour moved by more than 45 levels is outlined in magenta as the out-of-gamut warning (the vivid blue star moves from #1E5BFF to about #464B98). This is an emulation of what the preview shows, not the preview itself: the real Proof Colors toggle and the single-plate views stay manual.

steps.script:
import os
ps = doc.PDFSettings
ps.Reset()
ps.PublishRange = 1
ps.pdfVersion = 10
ps.IncludeBleed = False
ps.CropMarks = False
ps.EmbedFonts = True
ps.SubsetFonts = True
pdf = os.path.join(out, "press.pdf")
doc.PublishToPDF(pdf)
fonts, linked, embedded = [], 0, 0
for i in range(1, layer.Shapes.Count + 1):
    sh = layer.Shapes.Item(i)
    if sh.Type == 6:
        f = sh.Text.Story.Font
        if f not in fonts:
            fonts.append(f)
    elif sh.Type == 5:
        if sh.Bitmap.ExternallyLinked:
            sh.Bitmap.ResolveLink()
            linked += 1
        else:
            embedded += 1
pdf_kb = round(os.path.getsize(pdf) / 1024)
lines = ["Package list", "press.pdf: PDF/X-4, page 1 only, fonts embedded and subset (%d KB)" % pdf_kb,
         "press.cdr: the CorelDRAW file, saved after the links were embedded",
         "Fonts used: " + ", ".join(fonts) + " (named only: the font file is not copied, its licence may not allow it)",
         "Images: %d linked (embedded now), %d already embedded" % (linked, embedded)]
with open(os.path.join(out, "package_list.txt"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    fh.write(chr(10).join(lines) + chr(10))
for i, text in enumerate(lines[1:]):
    t = layer.CreateArtisticText(0.0, 0.0, text, 0, -1, "Arial", 15)
    t.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#1A1A1A"))
    t.Outline.SetNoOutline()
    t.SetPosition(1.0, 2.5 - i * 0.45)
o = app.CreateStructSaveAsOptions()
o.EmbedICCProfile = True
o.Overwrite = True
doc.SaveAs(os.path.join(out, "press.cdr"), o)
print("package written:", sorted(os.listdir(out)))
result = s
steps.note: Package (script): the PDF/X-4 with fonts embedded and subset (page 1 only) is written into the run's output folder; the script lists the fonts and bitmaps the page uses and embeds any linked bitmap (Bitmap.ResolveLink; none here); a package list (package_list.txt) and a summary on the page record what the package holds; then the document is saved as press.cdr next to the PDF (Document.SaveAs with a StructSaveAsOptions). Read back: the folder holds press.pdf, press.cdr and package_list.txt; the PDF was checked in the file (one page, PDF/X-4 marker, one embedded subset font file). Limits: CorelDRAW's own Collect For Output has no object-model call, so this is a scripted equivalent; the font file itself is not copied (the font is named only, since its licence may not allow redistribution); the saved .cdr also carries the harness scene's hidden masters page.
